supersedes: The 13 October 2026 built-in generator set, which mixed glossy postcard renders with sculptural still lifes. Retained files remain on disk for the apps that still reference them until each app's own release replaces them.
direction: App Composer cut-paper screenprint: warm ivory paper #f4f0e8, graphite ink #252923, burnt orange #d95022 and signal orange #ff9b55, with one accent per app (Linkarooie lime #a5fd0e, Here / there burnt orange, Link Check teal #2f9fbd, Hello orange, Carry / forward violet #8b5cf6). Flat shapes, ink-lined paper edges, coarse screenprint grain, deliberate registration offset. No shading, perspective, gloss, 3D render look, gradients or glow.
commonDirection: Every tile holds one simple silhouette that still reads at 48 pixels, carries no text, numbers, logos, watermarks or user-interface chrome, and never presents a drawing as a screenshot. Product names are typeset in HTML, never baked into artwork.

generation.billing: Paid per generated image under the account's existing provider plan. The provider sets and can change its price; no price is asserted in this record. Review the provider's current listing before repeating a batch.
generation.keyHandling: scripts/generate-app-art.mjs reads FAL_AI_API_KEY (or FAL_KEY) from the environment only. The key is never printed, never written to a job manifest, never committed and never shipped to the browser. Job manifests record the prompt and request identity, not credentials.
rejected: Direction drafts (flare, 9 images): kept only as the comparison record. Direction A was chosen for silhouette, material warmth and family coherence; a geometric pictogram set and a third option were not used.

Recraft v4.1 vector marks (5 images): semantically uneven across apps and incoherent as a family at 24-48px. Replaced by hand-authored SVG marks in one grammar. Masters kept under .artwork/masters/marks/ as the comparison record.
First Linkarooie tile attempt (tile-linkarooie-v3): the ribbon coil read as a curled tail, not a link, at 48 pixels. Regenerated as tile-linkarooie-v4 with the link drawn separately from the animal.
corrections: A padlock was removed from an early Carry / forward mark because a lock implies a security guarantee the app's own acceptance gates do not yet make.
The Hello arrow was redrawn after review so the route line reads as entering the archway rather than leaving it.

assets.subject: A green paper kangaroo mid-hop beside a two-link burnt-orange paper chain.
A burnt-orange paper postbox with one ivory postcard slipping into its slot, stamped with a permission-green square.
A teal paper magnifier over an ivory page card holding a burnt-orange landscape panel above two text rules.
A burnt-orange paper archway with a graphite route line stepping through it.
A graphite paper suitcase beside a violet route line carrying two paper tags.

shareCards.method: Authored as local HTML (.artwork/og/share-card.html) and captured in Chromium at 1200x630. The tile image is placed as artwork; every product name, category, line of description and the App Composer lockup are typeset live in the font stack, never generated inside an image.
outputs: 1200x630 JPEG for Open Graph and X
shareCards.typography: Space Grotesk (SIL OFL, licence retained at public/brand/OFL-Space-Grotesk.txt).

marks.method: Hand-authored SVG in one geometry grammar, one per app, drawn on a 40-unit grid with a 4-unit stroke and currentColor ink so the same file serves dark, light and small sizes.
marks.verified: Rendered at 16, 24, 48, 64 and 128 pixels on the dark and light surfaces in Chromium before use.
marks.copiesInto: Each app owns its copy; each app keeps its own favicon, install icon and header.

screenshots.method: Real browser captures of the deployed apps through the Chromium session (Playwright), never generated images and never re-drawn interfaces.
screenshots.guard: The library labels each capture as a real screenshot with its capture date, and says the illustration beside it is identity artwork rather than a screen. Alt text describes the actual interface state in the capture.
